reviews.question: A body of mass 10 kg moving with a velocity of 1 m/s is acted upon by a force of 50 N for two seconds. The final velocity of the body will be —
reviews.explanation:
Given, Force (F) = 50 N
Mass (m) = 10 kg
Initial velocity (u) = 1 m/s
Final velocity (v) = ?
Time (t) = 2 s.
We know F = ma.
50 = 10 × a
 a = 50/10 = 5 m/s².
From the first equation of motion:
v = u + at
v = 1 + 5 × 2
v = 11 m/s.

reviews.question: Mathematical formulation of Newton's law in Engineering Mechanics:
reviews.explanation:
Force F = d(mv)/dt.
Linear momentum P = mv.
Now, force = rate of change of momentum.
F = dP/dt (rate of change of momentum).
F = Ṗ (rate of change of momentum).
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Force F = d(mv)/dt.
Linear momentum P = mv.
Now, force = rate of change of momentum.
F = dP/dt (rate of change of momentum).
F = Ṗ (rate of change of momentum).
reviews.note: All three are the same momentum form of Newton’s second law. Derivative and dot choices restored from the scanned source.

reviews.question: A body of 20 kg mass moving with a velocity of 2 m/s is acted upon by a force of 100 N for four seconds. The final velocity will be:
reviews.explanation:
m = 20 kg (moving body mass)
u = 2 m/s
F = 100 N
t = 4 s.
We know that F = ma.
a = F/m = 100/20 = 5 m/s².
∴ v = u + at
= 2 + 5 × 4 = 2 + 20
v = 22 m/s.

reviews.question: The velocity–time graph of a body is a straight line passing through the origin. If its slope is m, the distance travelled in time t would be:
reviews.explanation:
Draw the velocity (u)–time (t) graph.
Distance s = area under the velocity–time curve
= (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × t × u.
s = ut/2.
Given, slope m = u/t ⇒ u = mt,
or t = u/m.
Therefore s = u²/(2m).

reviews.question: A monkey of mass 40 kg climbs on a rope which withstands maximum tension 600 N. In which case will it break? Take g=10m/s² and ignore the rope’s mass.

options.c: Climbs up with uniform speed 5 m/s

reviews.explanation:
Given:
Monkey’s mass m = 40 kg
g = 10 m/s²
Maximum rope tension Tmax = 600 N
Monkey’s acceleration a = 6 m/s².
According to the second law:
T = mg + ma
T = m(g + a)
T = 40(10 + 6)
T = 640 N.
Since T > Tmax, or 640 > 600, the rope will break.
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Given:
Monkey’s mass (m) = 40 kg
g = 10 m/s
Maximum tension in rope, Tmax = 600 N
Acceleration due to monkey a = 6 m/s².
According to second law of motion:
T = mg + ma
T = m[g + a]
T = 40[10 + 6]
T = 640 N.
Since T > Tmax or (640 > 600) the rope will break in this case.
reviews.note: Independent tensions are640N,240N and400N respectively. Corrected the source’s speed unit m/s² to m/s and g’s unit to m/s².

reviews.question: The motion of an artificial satellite orbiting Earth at constant height is an example of:
reviews.explanation:
For a satellite of mass m orbiting at radius r from Earth’s center, gravity supplies centripetal acceleration.
v_orbit = √(GMearth/r).
Earth’s gravity is the only force. From Newton’s gravitation law:
F = GmMearth/r².

reviews.question: What is the weight of a woman inside a lift accelerating downward at9.8m/s²?
reviews.explanation:
Given mass m and downward acceleration a=9.8m/s².
Apparent weight=m(g−a)
=m(9.8−9.8)
=0, since g=9.8m/s².
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Given mass m and downward acceleration a=9.8m/s².
Apparent weight=m(g−a)
=m(9.8−9.8)
=0, since g=9.8m/s².
reviews.note: Intended weight is apparent weight/normal reaction, zero in free fall. Gravitational force mg remains nonzero.

reviews.question: The force acting along a circle’s radius towards its center is:
reviews.explanation:
The inward radial force on a body in circular motion is known as centripetal force.
Fc = mv²/r,
where r=radius, m=mass and v=speed.

reviews.question: In relative equilibrium with respect to a moving body, the projections of all real forces together with the______due to base acceleration sum to zero.
reviews.explanation:
D’Alembert’s principle of inertial forces:
For a particle in relative equilibrium with a moving body, the projections of all real forces together with inertia force due to base acceleration sum to zero on every axis.
Σ(i=1 to n) Fi + FI = 0,
where FI is the inertia force(−ma_base for a translating frame) and Fi is a real force.
reviews.sourceExplanation:
D’Alembert’s principle of Inertial forces:
In case of relative equilibrium of a particle with respect to a moving body, the algebraic sum of the projections, on any axis, of all real forces acting on the particle together with the “Inertia” due to base acceleration must be zero.
FI − Σ(i=1 to n) Fi = 0.
FI = Inertial force.
Fi = A real force.
reviews.note: Source prints FI−ΣFi=0 while calling FI inertia force, inconsistent with its verbal statement. Corrected to ΣFi+FI=0, FI=−ma_base.

reviews.question: Absolute acceleration in relative motion is the geometric sum of:
reviews.explanation: Absolute acceleration in relative motion is the geometric sum of base acceleration, supplementary acceleration and relative acceleration.

reviews.question: A motorist travels at90km/h when a light250m ahead turns red for12seconds. To pass without stopping just as it turns green, his speed then will be:
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Given u=90kmph=90×5/18=25m/sec; t=12sec, s=250.
Applying Newton’s law of motion:
s=ut+1/2 at².
250=25×12+(1/2)(a)×12².
a=−0.694m/sec².
Now applying Newton’s law of motion equation:
v=u+at.
v=25+(−0.694)(12).
v=16.67m/sec.
v=16.67×18/5=60kmph.
reviews.note: Source assumes constant deceleration; otherwise final speed is not unique. Under that assumption v=2s/t−u=60km/h. Corrected loose Newton-law attribution.

reviews.question: A car starts from rest on a circular track of radius9m with constant tangential acceleration3m/s². What is its resultant acceleration after2s?
reviews.explanation:
Given at=3m/s²,R=9m,t=2s.
Using v=u+at, v=0+3×2=6m/s.
Resultant a=√(ar²+at²).
Radial acceleration ar=v²/R=6²/9=4m/s².
Resultant a=√(4²+3²)=5m/s².
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Given at=3m/s²,R=9m,t=2sec,a=?
According to Newton’s first law,v=u+at.
v=0+3×2=6m/s.
a=√(ar²+at²).
Radial ar=v²/R=6²/9=4m/s².
Resultant a=√(4²+3²)=5m/s².
reviews.note: Independent perpendicular components are4 and3m/s². Source falsely attributes v=u+at to Newton’s first law.

reviews.explanation:
Lower-drop fall time=4/10=0.4s.
Its distance=(10/2)(0.4)²=0.8m.…(i)
Second drop is released1/4s=0.25s later.
Its fall time=0.4−0.25=0.15s.
Its distance=(1/2)gt²=5(0.15)²=0.1125m.…(ii)
Separation=0.8−0.1125=0.6875m.
None of the choices is correct.

reviews.question: A car initially at20m/s has acceleration a=10−t/2. Determine its maximum speed.
reviews.explanation:
Given u=20m/s,a=10−t/2.
Maximum forward velocity occurs at a=0,t=20s.
a=dv/dt.
∫a dt=∫dv.
∫(10−t/2)dt=∫dv.
10t−t²/4=v−20.
At20s:200−100=v−20.
v=120m/s.
reviews.sourceExplanation:
Given u=20m/s,a=10−t/2.
Maximum forward velocity occurs at a=0,t=20s.
a=dv/dt.
∫a dt=∫dv.
∫(10−t/2)dt=∫dv.
10t−t²/4=v−20.
At20s:200−100=v−20.
v=120m/s.
reviews.note: Acceleration changes sign at20s; independent integration gives maximum forward velocity120m/s. If extended forever, reverse speed would be unbounded.

reviews.question: A cylinder of massM and radiusR rolls down an incline of angleθ. Its axis acceleration is(g denotes gravity):
reviews.explanation:
If the rolling object is a solid cylinder:
a=g sinθ/(1+K²/R²).
I=MK²=(1/2)MR²,
so K²/R²=1/2.
a=g sinθ/(1+K²/R²)
=g sinθ/(1+1/2)
=(2/3)g sinθ.
reviews.sourceExplanation:
If the rolling object is a solid cylinder:
a=g sinθ/(1+K²/R²).
I=MK²=(1/2)MR²,
so K²/R²=1/2.
a=g sinθ/(1+K²/R²)

reviews.question: A particle is acted on byF(x)=−k/(2x²) along the positive x-axis. Initially x=1m,v=0. What is its velocity at x=0.5m? k=10⁻²N·m² and mass=10⁻²kg.
reviews.explanation:
F=−k/(2x²),k=m=10⁻² in the stated SI units.
a=F/m=−1/(2x²).
Because a depends on position,use a=v dv/dx:
v dv=−dx/(2x²).
Integrating from x=1,v=0:
v²/2=(1/2)(1/x−1),so v²=1/x−1.
At x=0.5,v²=1.
Speed=1m/s; signed velocity is−1m/s because motion is toward decreasingx.
No listed choice gives signed velocity. If velocity means speed,a is correct.
The printed direct integration of d²x/dt² with respect tox to get dx/dt is invalid.
reviews.sourceExplanation:
From Newton’s Second law the inertia force is F=m×1.
F(x)=−k/(2x²)=m ax.
ax=−k/(m×2x²)=−1/(2x²).
ax=d²x/dt²=−1/(2x²).
v(x)=dx/dt=1/(2x)+c.
Initially x=1m,v=0:0=1/2+c,so c=−1/2.
dx/dt=1/(2x)−1/2.
At x=0.5m:v=1/(2×0.5)−1/2=0.5m/s.
Note:The Commission has given answer option(a).
reviews.note: Source keyd is mathematically wrong. Commissiona matches speed1m/s, but signed velocity−1m/s is absent; preserved ambiguity and disabled grading.

V+40=10/(10/60).
V=20km/h.
